message_post.doc:
Post a new message in an existing thread, returning the new mail.message.

Extra keyword arguments will be used either
  • as default column values for the new mail.message record if they match mail.message fields;
  • propagated to notification methods if not;

name_search.doc:
Search for records that have a display name matching the given name pattern when compared with the given operator, while also matching the optional search domain (domain).

This is used for example to provide suggestions based on a partial value for a relational field. Should usually behave as the reverse of display_name, but that is not guaranteed.

This method is equivalent to calling ~.search with a search domain based on display_name and mapping id and display_name on the resulting search.

search_read.signature: (domain=None, fields=None, offset=0, limit=None, order=None, read_kwargs) -> list[ValuesType]
search_read.doc: Perform a search_fetch followed by a _read_format.

web_search_read.signature: (domain, specification, offset=0, limit=None, order=None, count_limit=None) -> dict[str, int | list[dict]]
web_search_read.doc: Perform a search followed by a structured read. Unlike the standard search_read(), web_search_read() can traverse relational fields to fetch nested field values in a single call.

write.doc:
Update all records in self with the provided values.

  • For numeric fields (~odoo.fields.Integer, ~odoo.fields.Float) the value should be of the corresponding type

  • For ~odoo.fields.Boolean, the value should be a python:bool

  • For ~odoo.fields.Selection, the value should match the selection values (generally python:str, sometimes python:int)

  • For ~odoo.fields.Many2one, the value should be the database identifier of the record to set

  • The expected value of a ~odoo.fields.One2many or ~odoo.fields.Many2many relational field is a list of ~odoo.fields.Command that manipulate the relation the implement. There are a total of 7 commands: ~odoo.fields.Command.create, ~odoo.fields.Command.update, ~odoo.fields.Command.delete, ~odoo.fields.Command.unlink, ~odoo.fields.Command.link, ~odoo.fields.Command.clear, and ~odoo.fields.Command.set.

  • For ~odoo.fields.Date and ~odoo.fields.Datetime, the value should be either a date(time), or a string.

    Warning

    If a string is provided for Date(time) fields, it must be UTC-only and formatted according to odoo.tools.misc.DEFAULT_SERVER_DATE_FORMAT and odoo.tools.misc.DEFAULT_SERVER_DATETIME_FORMAT

  • Other non-relational fields use a string for value
